step1_figure.circuit_type: CMOS Op-Amp with Output Buffer (Indirect Compensation)
step1_figure.description: Two-stage CMOS operational amplifier comprising a folded/cascode differential input stage (M1-M6), a push-pull class-AB output buffer (MON, MOP biased via floating current source MFCP/MFCN and M8/M9), and indirect feedback compensation (Cc = 240 fF connected from Vout to node N008 at the source of M2T) driving a 1 kOhm resistor and 10 pF capacitor load in inverting configuration (Figure 24.31).

equation.formula: A_OLDC = A1 * A2 = [gmn * (ro2 || ro4)] * [-(gmn_out + gmp_out) * (ron || rop)]
equation.explanation: Overall DC open-loop gain is the product of the first-stage cascode diff-amp gain A1 and the push-pull output buffer stage gain A2.
equation.assumptions: Unloaded or high-impedance loaded output; small-signal square-law MOSFET model in saturation.

sky130_expected.calculation:
1) First stage cascode gain: A1 ≈ 500 (54 dB) as given in text.
2) Push-pull second stage: W_mon = 500/2, W_mop = 1000/2, conducting I_D ≈ 100 µA.
   gm_n = sqrt(2 * 270µ * (500/2) * 100µ) = 3.67 mA/V.
   gm_p = sqrt(2 * 50µ * (1000/2) * 100µ) = 2.24 mA/V.
   gm_total = 5.91 mA/V.
   ro_n = 1 / (0.1 * 100µ) = 100 kΩ, ro_p = 100 kΩ => ro_out = 50 kΩ.
   Unloaded A2 = -gm_total * ro_out = -5.91m * 50k ≈ -295 V/V (or ~-31.6 V/V per Eq. 24.36 with lower ro).
   When driving R_L = 1 kΩ (Fig. 24.31): A2_loaded ≈ -gm_total * (ro_out || 1k) ≈ -5.91m * 980 Ω ≈ -5.8 V/V (15.3 dB).
3) Loaded AOLDC ≈ 500 * 5.8 ≈ 2900 (≈ 69 dB); unloaded AOLDC ≈ 15,800 (84 dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Under nominal 1.8V supply in SKY130, the cascode first stage provides 50-60 dB, while the push-pull buffer provides 15-25 dB depending on output resistive loading.

equation.formula: fun = AOLDC * f3dB ≈ gm1 / (2 * pi * Cc)
equation.explanation: With indirect compensation, the unity-gain frequency is determined by the input stage transconductance gm1 and the feedback compensation capacitor Cc.
equation.assumptions: Dominant pole approximation holds, single dominant pole determined by node 1 and Cc.

sky130_expected.calculation:
1) Input pair bias: I_tail = 30 µA, so I_D1 = 15 µA per transistor.
2) Device sizes: W/L = 50/2 = 25.
   gm1 = sqrt(2 * 270µ * 25 * 15µ) = 450 µA/V.
3) Compensation capacitor: Cc = 240 fF.
4) fun ≈ gm1 / (2 * pi * Cc) = 450e-6 / (2 * pi * 240e-15) ≈ 298 MHz.
Accounting for parasitic capacitances at node 1 and internal nodes, fun typically settles around 120 - 200 MHz (Fig. 24.30 indicates ~150 MHz).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Typical f_un with 240 fF indirect compensation capacitance in 130 nm CMOS is between 100 MHz and 250 MHz.

phase_margin.description: Phase margin of the open-loop amplifier at unity-gain frequency

equation.explanation: Phase margin ensures closed-loop stability and determines the step response damping and overshoot.
equation.assumptions: Loop opened with large AC inductor/resistor while preserving DC bias.

sky130_expected.calculation: Text on page 794 specifies: 'The phase-margin is roughly 70 degrees.' Indirect compensation eliminates the right-half plane zero present in standard Miller compensation and moves the non-dominant pole to higher frequencies, yielding robust phase margin.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Well-compensated indirect topology targeted at 70° phase margin per textbook specification.

slew_rate_positive.description: Positive slew rate during low-to-high transition

equation.explanation: Rate of change when the input is pulsed high and the diff-amp tail current Iss charges the compensation capacitor Cc.
equation.assumptions: Output stage sourcing current is not limiting.

sky130_expected.calculation: Iss ≈ 30 µA, Cc = 240 fF => SR+ ≈ 30 µA / 240 fF = 125 V/µs (or 8.3 V/µs if Iss=20 µA, Cc=2.4 pF as on page 787). For Fig. 24.21/24.29 with Cc=0.24 pF, the text notes settling is under 10 ns for a 400 mV step.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The small indirect compensation capacitor (240 fF) enables very fast charging during positive slewing.

slew_rate_negative.description: Negative slew rate during high-to-low transition

equation.explanation: Rate of change when the output discharges the load capacitance and compensation capacitor.
equation.assumptions: Limited by the sinking current capacity of the pull-down network.

sky130_expected.calculation: From page 788: with 10 µA discharge current and 1.24 pF total capacitance, SR- ≈ 8 mV/ns = 8 V/µs. With push-pull output stage MON (W=500/2) capable of sinking higher peak current into 10 pF, SR- typically ranges between 10 V/µs and 30 V/µs.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Driving a 10 pF load requires significant current sinking; push-pull driver provides dynamic boost over a simple current sink.

equation.explanation: Ratio of differential-mode gain to common-mode gain, determined primarily by the input differential stage.
equation.assumptions: Symmetric diff-pair with finite output impedance of tail current source.

sky130_expected.calculation: As given on page 789: 'For the op-amps discussed so far in this chapter, the CMRR is approximately 50 dB (see Ex. 22.7, where the common-mode voltage is 500 mV)'. With cascoded tail source (xm6t, xm6b), CMRR is improved to 55-75 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Cascode tail source provides very high common-mode impedance, elevating CMRR above 50 dB.

psrr_positive.description: Power Supply Rejection Ratio from VDD (PSRR+)

equation.explanation: Ratio of differential open-loop gain to the gain from positive power supply noise to the output.
equation.assumptions: Measured with AC ripple superimposed on VDD supply.

sky130_expected.calculation: At low frequency, vout/v+ ≈ 1 (0 dB) per Fig. 24.27c, while AOLDC ≈ 70-80 dB. Thus PSRR+(DC) ≈ AOLDC - 0 dB ≈ 70 to 80 dB. Indirect compensation keeps PSRR high across frequency by isolating the compensation capacitor from VDD.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Cascode current sources and indirect feedback isolation from power rails ensure high PSRR.

source.reference: Text on p. 794 regarding output buffer current and diff-amp bias

equation.formula: P_DC = VDD * I_total = VDD * (I_bias_gen + I_diff + I_cascode + I_output)
equation.explanation: Static power consumption from VDD under quiescent DC conditions.
equation.assumptions: Inputs held at nominal common-mode voltage (0.9 V or 0.5 V).

sky130_expected.calculation:
VDD = 1.8 V.
Output stage conducts ~100 µA (p. 794).
Diff-amp tail conducts ~30 µA.
Cascode reference and bias generator branches draw ~40 µA.
Total current I_total ≈ 170 - 250 µA.
P_DC = 1.8 V * 200 µA ≈ 360 µW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Quiescent currents across all branches sum to approximately 150 - 300 µA on a 1.8V supply.

step3_testbench.description: Comprehensive ngspice testbench characterizing the CMOS op-amp with output buffer (Fig. 24.29). Measures DC operating power, open-loop gain and phase margin via a high-impedance feedback loop, closed-loop transient step response (settling time and slew rate) driving 1k || 10pF (Fig. 24.31), CMRR, and PSRR.
